page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 45 physical cores with multithreading enabled, alongside 177.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a resource density of approximately 1.97 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c3d-highcpu-90 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU execution and PassMark CPU tests. Its computational efficiency is further highlighted by top-tier results in software compilation with Clang and ray tracing workloads. Cryptographic and extended instruction tests also rank in the top 10%. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng single-core tests, while memory read bandwidth reaches up to 215.31 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, memory write bandwidth for large blocks and single-threaded compression tasks remain in the average tier.

The instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving. It also performs well in database operations and Redis deployments, achieving 116.26 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. For machine learning, the platform delivers top-tier prompt processing speeds for small LLM models, though text generation speeds for larger models fall into the average range due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff for I/O-heavy database workloads.
